reforms.description: The federal government announced an additional C$1.3 billion programme for science and technology over the next five years, aimed at enhancing research and innovation capacity. This includes a proposal to double the C$250 million spent on job training under the unemployment insurance programme, along with additional funding for existing programmes addressing skill shortages and measures to encourage R&D to boost competitiveness.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: The funding is intended to enhance research and innovation capabilities, which typically supports economic growth.
reforms.status_evidence: The programme was announced and is stated to be implemented.
reforms.importance_rationale: The reform represents a significant but narrower funding initiative rather than a structural overhaul.
reforms.source_quote: However, it proposed a doubling of the C$250 million spent on job training under the unemployment insurance programme, C$300 million more for existing programmes dealing with skill shortages, a new training tax and tax concessions to promote private sector worker training, national standards for redundancy notice and minimum severance pay, as well as measures to encourage R&D to boost competitiveness.
reforms.cross_verification_note: The description mentions an additional C$1.3 billion programme for science and technology aimed at enhancing research and innovation capacity, which aligns with direct public R&D funding.

reforms.description: The Canadian government introduced a refundable R&D tax credit for small firms and broadened the definition of R&D for tax purposes to include immediate write-off of all current and capital expenditures.
reforms.component_name: R&D Tax Credit for Small Firms
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: These tax incentives are designed to encourage private sector investment in R&D, which can lead to innovation and economic growth.
reforms.status_evidence: The reforms were introduced and are stated to be implemented.
reforms.importance_rationale: The introduction of tax credits and broadening of definitions represents a significant change in the tax treatment of R&D.
reforms.source_quote: Definition broadened to include immediate write-off of all current and capital expenditures.
reforms.cross_verification_note: The reform introduces a refundable R&D tax credit for small firms and broadens the definition of R&D for tax purposes, which qualifies as an innovation instrument for firms.

reforms.description: Canada introduced a refundable R&D tax credit for small firms and broadened the definition of R&D for tax purposes to include immediate write-off of all current and capital expenditures, rationalising the tax and grant system for R&D.
reforms.package_name: 1988 Canadian Science and Technology Investment Package
reforms.component_name: R&D Tax Credit and Definition Expansion
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: R&D tax credits and broadened definitions reduce the cost of R&D for firms, incentivising private investment in innovation and improving allocative efficiency.
reforms.status_evidence: Text states 'Canada introduced a refundable R&D tax credit', indicating implementation.
reforms.importance_rationale: Significant reform to the R&D tax system targeting small firms, but narrower in scope than a system-wide overhaul; part of a broader rationalisation package.
reforms.source_quote: Science and technology policy: a) Rationalise tax and grant system for R&D. Began to rationalise system. Introduced refundable R&D tax credit for small firms. b) Broaden definition of R&D for tax purposes. Definition broadened to include immediate write off of all current and capital expenditures.
reforms.cross_verification_note: This reform also introduces a refundable R&D tax credit for small firms and broadens the definition of R&D for tax purposes, qualifying it as an innovation instrument for firms.
